maplore

maplore adds components to mapgl maps that help readers understand what they are looking at: as they pan and zoom, the map tells them how the area in view compares with the rest.

Animated map of Argentina coloured by projected population growth. As the map is panned and zoomed, the summary panel on the left and the ranking on the right update with the departments in view, and hovering over a department shows a tooltip with its rank and its difference with the average
  • add_view_summary(): what is in view, compared with the whole map.
  • add_view_ranking(): which features stand out in view.
  • add_context_tooltip(): whether a value is high or low, and its rank.
  • add_feature_search(): find a place in your own data.

Everything runs in the browser, so it works in HTML pages, R Markdown and Quarto documents and dashboards, with no Shiny server.

Installation 

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("JMTocho/maplore")

Example 

library(mapgl)
library(maplore)

maplibre(center = c(-64, -38.5), zoom = 3.4) |>
  add_fill_layer(
    id = "departments",
    source = ar_departments,
    fill_color = interpolate(
      column = "growth",
      values = c(-10, 0, 10),
      stops = c("#b2182b", "#f7f7f7", "#2166ac")
    )
  ) |>
  add_view_summary("departments", "growth", name_column = "department", suffix = "%") |>
  add_context_tooltip("departments", "growth", name_column = "department", suffix = "%")

Learn more

The website explains each component, the included datasets and how maplore works.

maplore is experimental, and its functions may still change. Feedback and bug reports are welcome in the issues.

Much of the code was written with the help of an AI assistant (Claude, by Anthropic) and reviewed, tested and checked against independent calculations in R.
